interpretations.rationale: Final revision of this question, now with completed comparisons for the end-to-end demonstration. Receipt 585e5aba2b094fc980731545cd6cc3e6 (experiment 5e447681f32f4bd982a11690ef2cf54d-experiment) ran in the isolated workspace; status completed, outcome tests_passed, exit 0, no changed target files, no parsing errors. Decisive parsed indices: 0 is the admission and applicability record (StateLeader, joint true with voters [1 2 3] and outgoing [1 2 3], committed 2, applied 2, pendingConfIndex 2, already_pending false), 1 is the probe (entry_index 3, entry_type EntryConfChangeV2, committed 3, committed_reached true) and 2 is the apply (panicked true, panic config is already joint, still_joint true). All three declared comparisons evaluated holds with comparison_complete true, no missing indices and no diagnostics, which also removes the earlier caveat that the previous network receipt's comparisons were unknown because of duplicate event names - the harness now holds one case with unique names. The asserted defect, with its measured support: in a joint configuration, with no configuration change pending unapplied, propose-time validation in stepLeader derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 and therefore raises no failed check for an empty change set, so a ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition is accepted and replicated as an EntryConfChangeV2; that entry commits, and applying it - the documented action for a committed change the application does not reject - panics with config is already joint because applyConfChange asks ConfChangeV2.LeaveJoint, which for an empty change set is true only for the Auto transition, and so takes the EnterJoint branch that Changer.EnterJoint rejects on an already-joint configuration. The Auto-transition empty change remains the working control: it takes the LeaveJoint path and leaves the joint configuration without panicking. The pending-conf guard is recorded as a precondition rather than a mitigation of this defect: it applies when a configuration change is in the log but not yet acknowledged as applied, in which case the entry is rewritten to EntryNormal and this defect is not reached - which is exactly what happened in the earlier variant of the network test before I simulated application progress with appliedTo. Boundaries kept: application progress was simulated with raftLog.appliedTo(committed) rather than the full Ready and Advance loop; the consequence is a process panic in the application's ApplyConfChange call, with no state corruption, data loss or safety violation claimed; an application that rejects the change instead of applying it avoids the panic; and only the library's three transition values were covered, in one joint-configuration shape, with a joint state reached via AutoLeave not exercised.

knowledge.assertion: the malformed change survives validation as EntryConfChangeV2, commits, and panics on apply in a real three-node network
the pending-conf guard is the reason the un-acknowledged variant dropped the change as EntryNormal
with the guard inactive the explicit and implicit forms were accepted and panicked, while the Auto form left the joint configuration cleanly

limitations: Application progress was simulated by calling raftLog.appliedTo(committed) on each peer rather than driving Ready and Advance, though that is the effect those calls have.

The claimed consequence is a process panic in the application's ApplyConfChange call; no state corruption, data loss or safety violation is claimed, and an application that rejects the change avoids the panic.
The defect requires pendingConfIndex <= raftLog.applied at propose time; a lagging application is protected by the guard, and no claim is made about how often applications lag.
Only the three transition values the library defines were covered, in the explicit joint-configuration shape; a joint state reached through AutoLeave was not exercised.
Whether any given client emits a non-Auto transition with zero changes was not examined; the finding is that the library accepts such a change and then panics on the documented apply path.
